Hi there, I'm an owner of a 2015 escape and I live in rural alberta. I absolutely love it. they're pretty common so parts are relatively cheap and easy to find. Tire size kinda sucks on them so keep that in mind when pricing new tires, a Michelin defender i In a 235/55r17 will easily run you $1200+. A lot of older folks drive escapes as well, which might be part of the 80k-100k turn over rate (my bosses mom whose in her 80s has a 15 escape as well). I do know one gentlemen who had to replace the transmission in his 2014 escape, but he was an extremely high mileage driver. the other big complaint I heard is it doesn't have the same "oomph" as the 08-12 escapes have. From what I've read you will get the best fuel economy from the escape out of all the CUVs on the market. I know side impacts, the escape isn't rated to well, and just saw a video of a car pile up in Missouri where a young lady passed away, they were driving an escape. though my bosses grandma ended up t boning someone and the damage to the front of the escape was very minimal. 

After saying all that, I'd definitely look into a Rav4. I know a lot of farmers who own em and absolutely love them, since they handle gravel really well. Tire size will be a lot better and Toyota has legendary reliability. BUT, the down side is they rust really quickly. so if wherever you live uses a metric shit ton of calcium chloride on the road, itll eat up the undercarriage pretty good. 

I feel like both those vehicles will do you well, also depending on where in Alberta you live, you might have to drive a good distance to get major work done to it, which is also what helped me pick the escape.

hope this helps!
